edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Si haec ita se habent, ut veritas nobis adjudicetur, quicumque in ea regula incedimus quam Ecclesia ab Apostolis, Apostoli a Christo, Christus a Deo tradidit, constat ratio propositi nostri, definientis non esse admittendos haereticos ad ineundam de Scripturis provocationem, quos sine Scripturis probamus ad Scripturas non pertinere. Si enim haeretici sunt, christiani esse non possunt, non a Christo habendo quod de sua electione sectati haereticorum nomine admittunt. Ita non christiani, nullum jus capiunt christianarum litterarum. Ad quos merito dicendum est: Qui estis? quando, et unde venistis? quid in meo agitis, non mei? quo denique, Marcion, jure sylvam meam caedis? qua licentia, Valentine, fontes meos transvertis? qua potestate, Apelles, limites meos commoves? Quid hic caeteri ad voluntatem vestram seminatis et pascitis? Mea est possessio; olim possideo: habeo origines firmas, ab ipsis auctoribus quorum fuit res. Ego sum haeres Apostolorum. Sicut caverunt testamento suo, sicut fidei commiserunt, sicut adjuraverunt, ita teneo. Vos certe exhaeredaverunt semper et abdicaverunt, ut extraneos, ut inimicos. Unde autem extranei et inimici Apostolis haeretici, nisi ex diversitate doctrinae, quam unusquisque de suo arbitrio adversus Apostolos, aut protulit, aut recepit?
pass_a_gloss: If these things are so, that truth is adjudged to us, whoever we are who walk in that rule which the Church received from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, Christ from God handed down, it is established the reason of our proposal, defining that heretics are not to be admitted to undertaking a challenge about the Scriptures, whom we prove without the Scriptures not to pertain to the Scriptures. For if they are heretics, they cannot be Christians, not having from Christ what they admit to having followed in the election of heretics by name. Thus not being Christians, they take no right of Christian writings. To whom it is to be said with merit: Who are you? when, and from where have you come? what are you doing in my matter, not mine? by what right, finally, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? with what license, Valentine, do you divert my springs? with what power, Apelles, do you move my boundaries? What are the rest of you sowing and feeding here according to your will? Mine is the possession; I have long been in possession: I have firm origins, from the very authors whose matter it was. I am the heir of the Apostles. Just as they took precautions by their will, just as they entrusted to faith, just as they adjured, so I hold. You, certainly, have always been disinherited and disowned, as strangers, as enemies. But from where are heretics strangers and enemies to the Apostles, if not from the diversity of doctrine, which each one either produced or received from his own judgment against the Apostles?

choices.english: the Church received from the Apostles
rejected: the Church handed down to the Apostles

choices.why: showing the origin of the tradition

pass_b_english: If this is how things stand—that truth is awarded to us who walk the rule the Church received from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, and Christ from God—then the rationale behind our position is settled: heretics must not be admitted to a contest over Scripture. We have already proved, without using Scripture, that they have no connection to it. If they are heretics, they cannot be Christians; they possess nothing from Christ, yet they embrace the very name that marks their chosen faction. Not being Christians, they hold no right to Christian writings. So we are fully justified in demanding: Who are you? When and from where did you come? What are you doing in what is mine, not yours? By what right, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? By what license, Valentinus, do you divert my springs? By what power, Apelles, do you move my boundary markers? What are the rest of you doing, sowing and pasturing here at your own pleasure? This possession is mine; I have held it for a long time. My title is solid, traced back to the very authors whose work it was. I am the Apostles' heir. Just as they safeguarded it in their testament, just as they entrusted it to the faith, just as they swore it into force, so I hold it. You, on the other hand, have always been disinherited and disowned—strangers, enemies. And how else could heretics be strangers and enemies to the Apostles except through a divergence of doctrine that each one either invented or adopted on his own authority in opposition to the Apostles?

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex chain of transmission (Ecclesia -> Apostoli -> Christus -> Deus). Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of 'sicut caverunt testamento suo' (just as they safeguarded it in their testament) compared to Pass A's 'took precautions by their will', which is a slight interpretive stretch of 'caverunt', but Pass B remains faithful to the sense. The rhetorical questions and the specific names (Marcion, Valentine, Apelles) are correctly rendered.

The translation accurately reflects the Latin text, preserving the meaning, structure, and intent of the original passage. All key terms and concepts are correctly rendered in English, and the citations and references are consistent with the source material.
